recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing process handoff with identity state transfer (new binary).
justification: dependency/toolchain/runtime/native/embedded change needs a new binary; S5 keeps the listening socket and transfers state unchanged (state schema identical)

goroutine-structure, long-running or start-up code changed: in-process patching would leave old code running in goroutines that never return; a new process starts the new goroutine structure, and the old one is drained and exits

S6 blockers (14): cloud.google.com/go/monitoring: dependency graph changed; cloud.google.com/go/trace: dependency graph changed; contrib.go.opencensus.io/exporter/jaeger: dependency graph changed; contrib.go.opencensus.io/exporter/stackdriver: dependency graph changed; github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go: dependency graph changed; ... and 9 more
alternatives: Kubernetes rolling update (loses in-memory state, needs surge capacity)
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo/src/frontend.main
2 of 3 patched functions have no context.Context parameter: they get per-call, not per-request, version consistency under S6
3 patched functions are in package main; a Go plugin cannot import package main, so hotpatchgen must relocate them into an importable package
type information is partial (415/392 type errors old/new; third-party packages are opaque): call-graph and state reachability are lower bounds
quiescence: old activations of main(), init-started or long-running goroutines never return, so the old process is retired by exit, not by draining; set a drain deadline in the S5 upgrader
